groups.title: Intransitive VNC structure
groups.writingJob: Build an intransitive VNC as #pers1-pers2(STEM)tns+num1-num2# while keeping Valence grammatically present but vacant.
groups.readingJob: Show how Subject and Predicate surround the stem and explain that unwritten Valence is still grammatically present.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies an intransitive source or valence; the application selects the intransitive formula and preserves its implicit Valence position.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the Source VNC Valence choice. Do not add a formula or empty-Valence control.
groups.proposal: Make the intransitive formula the automatic normal Result for an intransitive VNC source.

groups.title: Morphs, carriers, and spelling
groups.writingJob: Keep a grammatical morph distinct from its spoken, written, or silent carrier, and do not turn spelling variants into separate grammar.
groups.readingJob: Explain regular variants, real morphic variants, spelling variants, silent carriers, and Andrews's slash and tilde notation.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the intended source; the application preserves morph identity and chooses its contextual carrier and spelling.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add a spelling-variant control. Contextual realization and notation are application and reading-guide duties.
groups.proposal: Make morph identity part of the typed analysis while treating spelling as its contextual realization.

groups.title: Subject person forms
groups.writingJob: Select the authorized pers1 subject filler, supportive i, optative x, and second-plural nasal realization from person, number, mood, and the following sound.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader recover person and number from pers1 even where visible forms are homophonous or assimilated.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses subject person and number; the application derives supportive vowels, optative forms, assimilation, and the disambiguating number suffix.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the subject control. Do not expose supportive vowels, nasal assimilation, or pers1 allomorphs as separate choices.
groups.proposal: Make subject person and number the only user choices while the application realizes the exact pers1 carrier.

groups.title: Subject case and silent nominative
groups.writingJob: Fill pers2 with the silently present nominative zero morph for every VNC subject.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader see silent nominative case as a real grammatical morph rather than an absence of grammar.
groups.decisionSplit: The subject function determines nominative case; the application supplies pers2=0 automatically.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add a case control for an ordinary VNC subject.
groups.proposal: Keep nominative case structurally present and automatically realized by zero.

groups.title: Subject number connector
groups.writingJob: Choose num1 from tense, mood, verbstem class, following number, and the licensed regular, supportive, or silent realization.
groups.readingJob: Show that c, qu, qui, and square zero are number-connector realizations rather than tense morphs.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses grammatical tense, mood, and subject number; the application derives num1.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add a number-connector or silent-variant control.
groups.proposal: Make num1 an automatic bridge between the predicate and final subject number.

groups.title: Definitive subject number suffix
groups.writingJob: Realize singular or common number with zero and select h, eh, an, in, or ih for plural from the active mood-tense pattern.
groups.readingJob: Use num2 as the definitive number locus and read its variant together with num1.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses subject number; the application derives the licensed num2 carrier.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the subject-number choice. Do not expose suffix variants separately.
groups.proposal: Make num2 the final automatic statement of subject number.

groups.title: Complete VNC subject paradigms
groups.writingJob: Build every subject person-number form through the four Canvas mood-tense paradigms, including common third person and all licensed silent variants.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader from a complete subject dyad to its possible participant interpretation without importing English gender into Nahuatl grammar.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses subject, mood, and tense; the application selects the paradigm and complete distributed subject form.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse subject, mood, and tense. Do not add a paradigm-number picker.
groups.proposal: Make the four paradigms automatic consequences of ordinary grammatical choices.

groups.title: Verbstem meaning, valence, voice, and aspect
groups.writingJob: Keep lexical meaning, valence, voice, and aspect in the verbstem and require a real perfective realization even where its formation is not predictable.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through active and nonactive voice, imperfective and perfective aspect, and the eight contrasting stem kinds.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a genuine construction or voice where available; lexical stem facts and required aspect shape remain application duties.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source, valence, voice, and applicable derivation controls. Never offer evidence absence as a no-form choice.
groups.proposal: Make the typed verbstem the source of lexical meaning and all required stem-category distinctions.

groups.title: Mood, tense, aspect, and tense morphs
groups.writingJob: Allow only the Canvas mood-tense-aspect combinations and realize the exact tense morph in the tns slot.
groups.readingJob: Distinguish grammatical tense from real-world time and preserve the licensed translation ranges and ambiguous silent-number dyad.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a genuine mood and tense; the application limits choices by aspect and class and supplies the tns carrier.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse mood and tense controls with Canvas-based availability. Do not expose tense morphs or English translations as grammar choices.
groups.proposal: Make mood and tense genuine choices whose available combinations and morphs are enforced by the application.
